description: THE EMPTY CROSS REFERENCE, and the whole-run counterpart of case06's single miss: XREFFILE is seeded with NO ROW AT ALL, so every one of the three records misses and 3000-READ-ACCOUNT at app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl:241-250 is NEVER PERFORMED ONCE for the entire run. 2000-LOOKUP-XREF at :227-239 takes its INVALID KEY arm on every call, so :232 displays 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOR XREF' and :233 moves 4 into WS-XREF-READ-STATUS; the mainline test at :173 is therefore FALSE on every iteration and the ELSE arm at :180-184 - one DISPLAY with four operands - runs in its place every time. That is what this case proves and case06 cannot: the account code path can be bypassed for a COMPLETE run without the program faltering, and the run still ends normally. The two arms are asserted in source order, which is what gate G30 asks of an ordered IF, and here the :173 IF is the arm NEVER taken while the :180 ELSE is taken on every iteration - the exact inverse of the clean path in case01. Gate G47 is satisfied at two call sites rather than one: the keyed read of the cross reference reports '23' record-not-found on all four calls (FileStatus.NOT_FOUND, surfaced through CardXrefRepository.ReadResult.notFound rather than abended), while the sequential read of the daily file reports '00' three times and then '10'. SEEDS. dailytran.txt rows 1, 2 and 3 are seeded in file order, carrying DALYTRAN-ID 0000000000683580, 0000000001774260 and 0000000006292564 at bytes 1-16 and DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM 4859452612877065, 0927987108636232 and 6009619150674526 at bytes 263-278. XREFFILE is declared with an EXPLICIT EMPTY COLLECTION - "empty": true together with its CVACT03Y recordLength of 50 - and that is a different assertion from both of its neighbours, in two directions. It is not an OMITTED member: an omitted dataset is one the case says nothing about, and a run that read it would read nothing while nobody could tell whether that was intended. And it is not an UNBOUND dataset: a dataset with no binding fails its OPEN at :291 and displays 'ERROR OPENING CROSS REF FILE', which is the open-failure scenario and belongs to case19, not here. An empty SEEDED dataset opens successfully with status '00' at :292, and every keyed read against it then misses. Confusing the two turns this case into a different one, which is why the declaration is explicit rather than inferred (practice B8). acctdata.txt row 7 is seeded at its full 300 bytes and the choice of row is the point: its ACCT-ID is 00000000007, which is exactly the XREF-ACCT-ID that card 4859452612877065 - row 1's card - resolves to in the real cross reference at cardxref.txt row 21. So the account this run would have read IS PRESENT AND COMPLETE, and the absence of every account line below is attributable to the empty cross reference ALONE rather than to a missing account. A translation that skipped the account read for the wrong reason, or that pre-read the account before consulting the cross reference, cannot hide behind an absent row. CUSTFILE, CARDFILE and TRANFILE are declared empty at their copybook widths - CVCUS01Y 500, CVACT02Y 150 and CVTRA05Y 350 - because :158, :160 and :162 open them and :189, :191 and :193 close them while no READ in the program ever touches them; the only reads are DALYTRAN at :203, XREF-FILE at :229 and ACCOUNT-FILE at :243, and the last of those never executes here. Declaring them is a positive statement that three real datasets were opened and held no row, which omitting them could not make. EMPTINESS IS EXPRESSED IN THE CASE, NEVER ON DISK (practice B3): app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt still holds all fifty of its rows and is not emptied, truncated or edited by one byte, and neither is anything else under app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/jcl, app/proc or app/data. They are the parity oracle and they are read-only. This matters because all 50 distinct card numbers in dailytran.txt resolve in the unmodified cardxref.txt and every account they cross-refer to exists in acctdata.txt, so a total miss cannot arise from the full fixtures and is manufactured solely by what this case declines to SEED. MESSAGES - thirteen lines, in this order, and no fourteenth. The arithmetic is exact: each of the three records contributes an echo plus a two-line miss group, the post-end-of-file pass contributes a two-line miss group with no echo, and the two banners bracket the lot, so 3x3 + 2 + 2 = 13. :156 opens with the start banner. Each :168 line is the raw 350-byte DALYTRAN-RECORD image, FILLER X(20) included, byte-identical to the seeded row it echoes. Each miss group is :232's fixed literal followed by the single four-operand DISPLAY at :181-183, which is ONE line and not three - 'CARD NUMBER ' with the trailing space inside the literal, then DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM as sixteen untrimmed characters, then ' COULD NOT BE VERIFIED. SKIPPING TRANSACTION ID-' with its leading space inside the literal and ending on the hyphen with no trailing space, then DALYTRAN-ID as sixteen untrimmed characters, concatenated with no separator beyond the literals' own spaces. ENTRIES 11 AND 12 ARE THE POST-END-OF-FILE LOOKUP, and they are asserted rather than trimmed (practice B5). The loop at :164-186 iterates a fourth time; the READ at :203 reports '10', so :217 moves 'Y' into END-OF-DAILY-TRANS-FILE; the inner guard at :167 closes at :169 and covers ONLY the DISPLAY at :168, so the record echo is suppressed - which is why there is NO ECHO BETWEEN ENTRY 10 AND ENTRY 11 - while the three statements at :170-172 sit OUTSIDE that guard and run anyway, on the DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM and DALYTRAN-ID the record area still holds, because a READ ... INTO does not disturb its receiving area AT END. The stale values are ROW 3's, not row 1's, so entries 11-12 repeat entries 9-10 verbatim and carry card 6009619150674526 with id 0000000006292564. A run therefore performs recordsRead + 1 lookups - four here for three records - always. Hoisting :170-172 inside the guard makes this case fail, and so does reusing the FIRST record's key instead of the last, which is exactly the pair of mistakes the arrangement invites. ABSENT BY DESIGN, and asserted absent by an expectation list that names every line: no 'SUCCESSFUL READ OF XREF' (:235), no 'CARD NUMBER: ' / 'ACCOUNT ID : ' / 'CUSTOMER ID: ' block (:236-238), no 'SUCCESSFUL READ OF ACCOUNT FILE' (:249), no 'INVALID ACCOUNT NUMBER FOUND' (:246) and no line composed as :178 composes it - 'ACCOUNT ' then ACCT-ID then ' NOT FOUND'. The last two are the subtle ones and they are why the account row is seeded at all. :175 never executes, so ACCT-ID is never assigned; 3000-READ-ACCOUNT never runs, so neither of its two arms can report anything; and the not-found line at :178 is unreachable for the same reason. A translation that reported an account as not found - which is the plausible mistake when nothing resolves - emits a line this case does not list and fails, even though the account file it would have been reading holds a real, matching record. On an INVALID KEY the READ ... INTO at :229 also leaves CARD-XREF-RECORD untouched, so XREF-CUST-ID and XREF-ACCT-ID keep whatever they held - here nothing at all - and neither field is DISPLAYed on this path, so that has no observable effect and must produce no line. expectedWrites is EMPTY as a positive assertion, not an absence of interest: the source contains zero WRITE and zero REWRITE statements and all six SELECTs are opened OPEN INPUT (:254, :273, :291, :309, :327, :345), so posting is not merely absent but impossible, and the six WRITES-channel expectations say the same thing per dataset at its exact copybook width. expectedReturnCode is stated explicitly as 0 (practice B8), and this case is the strongest form of that claim in the folder: an ENTIRE RUN in which NOTHING resolves still completes normally. :233 moves 4 into WS-XREF-READ-STATUS, which is a local flag read once at :173 and never moved anywhere else, and CBTRN01C contains no MOVE targeting RETURN-CODE at all, so the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :473 is unreached and normal completion is 0. The temptation to make a total failure fail loudly must be resisted: the source does not, so neither does this case (practice B5). jobParameters is empty because CBTRN01C is the migration's ORPHAN: no EXEC PGM=CBTRN01C exists anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc, so there is no PARM for a parameter to come from and the job carries no trigger (requirement I4, gate G13). R1 and practice B4 caveat, documented and not 'fixed': the prompt-mandated class name TransactionPostingJob and the source's own 'Post the records from daily transaction file' header both promise posting, and the verified source posts nothing; the real POSTTRAN poster is CBTRN02C, which migrates as TransactionValidationJob. An expectation here that asserted a posted transaction record would be a behaviour change rather than a fix. WIDTHS. The two seeded datasets are pinned unchanged on the final-state channel at their copybook widths - DALYTRAN 350 from CVTRA06Y across all three rows, and ACCTFILE 300 from CVACT01Y - which is what proves every FILLER span was emitted (gates G19 and G21). The account row is pinned twice over on purpose: by whole-record image, and by three named spans - ACCT-ID, ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE, which keeps the copybook's own misspelling because renaming it would break field-for-field diffing (requirement I1), and the 178-byte FILLER at bytes 123-300, space-filled. XREFFILE has no row to pin and is asserted at row count zero on both channels instead, which is the whole subject of the case. GATE G16 IS NOT EXERCISED HERE, and the omission is deliberate rather than overlooked: the 36-to-50 CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD normalisation pads SEEDED cross-reference rows to CVACT03Y's absent FILLER X(14), and this case seeds none, so no pad can fire and none is declared - a normalisation naming a dataset the case declares empty is refused by the contract, correctly, because it would be an assertion nothing could ever check. case01 and case06 carry G16; this case carries the emptiness they cannot. BASELINE PROVENANCE, practice B12: these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl read paragraph by paragraph - :164-186 for the mainline arms and :227-239 for the keyed read - cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts in app/cpy (CVTRA06Y's DALYTRAN-ID at bytes 1-16 and DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM at 263-278, CVACT01Y's 300 bytes, CVACT03Y's 50, every offset mechanically diffable by eye - practice B11) and against the real ASCII fixtures, from which dailytran rows 1-3 and acctdata row 7 are COPIED VERBATIM rather than transcribed. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, because executing it is empirically impossible in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed-file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE* services, so CALL 'CEE3ABD' cannot be reached at all. AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers; the substitution changes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else, and is escalated for explicit user confirmation as risk R-A rather than silently absorbed. Bytes are US-ASCII, stated and never taken from the platform default (practice B8), and nothing here reads a clock, draws an unpredictable value or consults the environment - CBTRN01C reads no clock - so the fingerprint is identical on every run (practice B7). Nothing is a placeholder: three complete 350-character records, one complete 300-character record and all thirteen lines in full, and the empty XREFFILE is a real, deliberate value rather than a stand-in (practice B1). review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided.", so NO USER RULE governs this fixture; the binding standard is the enterprise-practice set B1-B12 of AAP section 0.10.2, and its absence is not licence to assert less. Gates carried: G13, G15, G18, G19, G21, G30, G47 and G51 - the unit is the tasklet body of transaction.TransactionPostingJob, invoked directly with no JobLauncher, no job repository, no HTTP layer and no application context in the path. G32 does not apply: CBTRN01C contains zero GO TO statements. G16 is not exercised, as set out above.
